processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Parent process step (proc_hot-rolled): laboratory-melted 50 kg ingot (Ø150 mm) homogenized at 1200 °C for 5 h.
Ingots were hot rolled into rods with a diameter of 16 mm then air-cooled to room temperature.
Main终态 used for tensile tests, Charpy impact toughness and EBSD/TEM characterization (process_id proc_st-1050c-2h-wq).

structures.overall_structure: After solution treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h + WQ the Al-12 (Fe30Mn12Al1C) steel consists mainly of a single austenite (FCC) matrix with a small amount of BCC ferrite phase (3.08% volume fraction) and finely distributed intragranular κ-carbides (~15 nm) in the austenite; a relatively fine austenite grain size (12.6 μm) is obtained relative to the other high-Al grades.
structures.number_of_phases: 2 (austenite FCC matrix + ferrite BCC), plus κ-carbide precipitates
structures.microstructure_counts: 1 austenite matrix phase; 1 minor ferrite phase; κ-carbide precipitates uniformly distributed

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix
precipitates.coherency: coherent with the austenite matrix (shear/particle-shear strengthening); orientation relationship (001)κ || (001)γ

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Twin boundary fraction f_Tw = 51.3% for the Al-12 steel

interfaces.slip_behavior: Shear deformation facilitates the glide of dislocations across κ-carbide shear planes; the κ-carbides are sheared by dislocations (particle shear model) even at sizes up to ~50 nm rather than bypassed by an Orowan mechanism.
interfaces.phase_evolution: With increasing Al from 8% to 12%, only austenite is present for 8–11% Al, whereas at 12% Al a small fraction of ferrite (3.08%) forms; κ-carbide precipitation goes from absent at 8% Al to ~15 nm at 12% Al.
interfaces.interface_notes: For the 12% Al steel, coherent κ-carbides (~15 nm) lie within the twinned austenite matrix, with a thin BCC ferrite fraction; no separate interphase crystallographic texture is reported.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: standard tensile specimens with gauge length of 25 mm and diameter of 5 mm; tensile axis parallel to the rod axis
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Two solution-treated specimens tested; data reported as the average of two specimens; stress-strain jumps after yielding caused by removal of the extensometer.

elongation.direction: parallel to rod axis (uniform elongation UE)
parallel to rod axis (elongation to failure A)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curves after 2 h solution treatment at 1050 °C are presented in Fig. 2(a-c); curve for the 12% Al steel reflects the Al-content series (no κ-carbide-free behaviour).
strain_hardening_rate: maximum work hardening rate ~2100 MPa for the 6%Al steel; work hardening rate decreases with increasing Al content, so the 12% Al steel has among the lowest hardening rates of the Al series

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Charpy impact specimens with the V-notch perpendicular to the rod axis (10 × 10 mm cross-section, V-notch 2 mm deep, 55 mm long)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: MTS impact tester (500 J capacity); data is the average of two solution-treated specimens

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: standard tensile specimens with gauge length of 25 mm and diameter of 5 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: σ_TS and FRS are single values (no scatter) derived via Eqns (1) and (2); A is the maximum area reduction measured from failed tensile specimens.

ultimate_tensile_strength.direction: true stress, maximum true stress just before necking (crack nucleation), σ_TS

service_conditions.stress_state: uniaxial tension (parallel to rod axis) and Charpy V-notch impact loading

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD system attached to a field emission gun scanning electron microscope (SEM, FEI Quanta 650, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Hillsboro, OR, USA); Channel 5 post-processing software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Operating voltage 20 kV; step size 0.5 μm; specimens mechanically ground and electro-polished in 7% Nital at room temperature; grain size by linear intercept method with 15° boundary misorientation definition
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase distribution (austenite/ferrite), grain size, and twin boundary fraction of the Al-12 steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Al-12 steel: single austenite matrix with a small BCC ferrite fraction of 3.08%, austenite grain size 12.6 ± 1.2 μm, twin boundary fraction f_Tw = 51.3%, ferrite grain size 4.5 ± 0.9 μm

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), dark-field imaging with SAED
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM, Tecnai G2 F20 S-TWIN, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Hillsboro, OR, USA
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Operating voltage 200 kV; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in 10% perchloric acid + 90% ethanol at 20 V and -20 °C; dark-field images taken along [001]γ zone axis using a κ-carbide reflection
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the size, distribution and crystallography of κ-carbides in the austenite matrix of the Al-12 steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: κ-carbides uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix with average diameter ~15 ± 6 nm for the 12% Al steel; no κ-carbides in 8% Al; orientation relationship (001)κ || (001)γ

characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the mass density of the alloy compositions

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical particle (shear) strengthening model for coherent κ-carbides
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Linear fitting of yield strength versus square root of κ-carbide size (Fig. 7a) gives a constant slope of 97.1 MPa/nm^1/2; the flow stress in the absence of κ-carbide strengthening was estimated as about 478 MPa.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relates the shear strength contribution to the κ-carbide volume fraction and average diameter: σ_shear = α f^(1/2) d_Car^(1/2)
analytical_models.model_note: Particle shear strengthening is suggested to remain active even for κ-carbide sizes up to 50 nm, much larger than the typical ~5 nm critical size for the shearing-to-Orowan transition.

analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts mass density from alloy content (mass%): ρ = 8.10 - 0.102C - 0.10Al - 0.01Mn g/cm3
analytical_models.model_note: Coefficients for Al and Mn are similar to previously reported values, but the C coefficient (0.102 g/cm3 per 1% C) is much smaller than the previously reported 0.41 g/cm3 per 1% C.

unmapped_findings: Al-12 (Fe30Mn12Al1C) is the highest-Al member of the Fe30Mn(x)Al1C series, with nominal chemistry C 1.02, Mn 30.47, Al 12.04, Fe balance (Table 1).
Nominal composition of the Al-12 steel: C 1.02 wt%, Mn 30.47 wt%, Al 12.04 wt%, Fe balance; measured density 6.52 g/cm3 by the Archimedes drainage method.

For the Al-12 steel, κ-carbide growth is rectangular/square in shape in the high-carbon case; the general orientation relationship between κ-carbides and austenite is (001)κ || (001)γ, and growth of κ-carbides took place with {011} as the growth plane (reported for the 1.5%C steel of the same series).

Both ultimate true stress (σ_TS ≈ 1350 MPa) and fracture true stress (σ_FS ≈ 2150 MPa) are nearly constant for all investigated compositions including Al-12, independent of κ-carbide size and microstructure; the origin of these constant values remains unexplained and is proposed for future work.

As a member of the Fe30Mn(x)Al1C series after 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment, the Al-12 steel produced the smallest austenite grain size (12.6 μm) of the Al series, a κ-carbide size of ~15 nm, and the lowest impact toughness (3.8 J), reflecting an Al content above 11% that strongly impairs impact toughness.
